newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Bank voices confidence in SAR property policy.
newsitem.headline: HK Bank voices confidence in SAR property policy.

text.p: Hongkong Bank executive director Vincent Cheng expressed confidence on Monday that Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa would be able to keep property prices under control in the territory.
"C.H. Tung has already said that housing is one of the priorities of his government and C.H. has a very strong business background," Cheng told Reuters in an interview.
"He understands how to keep property prices at a reasonable level, most importantly at an affordable level, because property or housing ownership is the key to the social stability of a place."
From July 1, Hong Kong will become a Special Administrative Region (SAR) of China, run by its chief executive Tung Chee-hwa.
Cheng said the answer to escalating property prices was for the government to release more land.
"We do have a large number of land in the New Territories for example which could be developed," Cheng said, referring to Hong Kong's rural districts.

"As long as we can quickly increase the supply of land and make those lands available for public developments, I hope that we could keep property prices down because if property prices continue to rise, our competitiveness will be affected."

But Cheng said the Hong Kong Monetary Authority was also "rightly concerned" about high property prices. "At the moment demand for property is still very strong and therefore I don't see how prices would come off," said Cheng.

The HKMA, the territory's defacto central bank, said last week that the current growth in mortgage lending was historically high and additional restraints in mortgage lending policies may be required.
The "M.A. is rightly concerned about high property prices and therefore they have issued warnings to banks hoping that banks should not be overexposed to that sector," said Cheng.
He said he hoped any guidelines issued by the HKMA would be balanced, giving banks the freedom to manage their own business.
